podcast.body: Weezer's cover of the Toto hit from 1982. The cover originated from a persistent request, or "demand," from a 14-year-old fan in Cleveland named Mary Kinchen, who tweeted at the band. After initially covering Toto's "Rosanna," Weezer eventually recorded "Africa," releasing it digitally and as a limited edition 7-inch single. "The song that got the most attention was Weezer's version of Africa, the total hit from 1982."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.body: Approximately one week after releasing their cover of "Rosanna," Weezer released their version of Toto's "Africa," which subsequently "blew up." It quickly soared to the top of the iTunes charts, received extensive radio play worldwide, and became Weezer's biggest hit in over a decade. "Weezer let that sink in for about a week and then suddenly posted their version of Africa. And it just blew up."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Weezer's 2018 cover of Toto's 1983 Hot 100 number one hit, "Africa." The cover was recorded as a direct response to a 14-year-old fan tweeting at frontman Rivers Cuomo and subsequently became Weezer's biggest rock radio hit in a decade. "Weasers cover of Totos 1983 Hot 100 number one, Africa, which by the way was recorded simply because a 14-year-old Weaser fan tweeted at Frontman Rivers Cuomo that the band should record Africa."
